penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A validated runbook or configuration guide for Cisco UCS Boot-from-SAN requires hands-on environment testing and expert review to be credible and safe — Claude cannot autonomously generate reliable, production-safe infrastructure runbooks for this stack without human validation.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling a $500–$5k engagement to an enterprise infrastructure team realistically requires a discovery call or at minimum asynchronous back-and-forth scoped to their specific UCS/SAN configuration — not a self-serve click-and-pay flow.

rationale: The pain is real and expensive (boot failures blocking production deployments in large IT environments), and the buyer has budget. However, this is an extremely narrow, infrequent problem — most sysadmins encounter it once per deployment project, not repeatedly. More critically, the solution cannot be automated: generating a reliable Boot-from-SAN runbook for a specific Cisco UCS + XtremIO configuration requires hands-on environment knowledge, vendor-specific testing, and expert review that Claude cannot safely provide autonomously. Lead reachability is also very poor — there is no public list of Cisco UCS admins to cold-outreach at scale.
solution_plan: This is not viable for an autonomous factory. The problem is too narrow, too infrequent, and too environment-specific for a self-serve automated product. Selling an infrastructure runbook into a large enterprise requires scoped discovery and human credibility that a solo non-technical operator cannot manufacture without domain expertise. Do not build.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (3 < 6) and operational_autonomy (3 < 7). Extremely low lead reachability. Drop.
